picks.what: Panorama, engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 1
picks.why: colored profile view of the whole town with St. Rumbold’s tower; trimmed to the Mechelen strip, the lowest of three city views on the plate; flat single sheet

picks.file: Gezicht op Mechelen Mechelen (titel op object), RP-P-AO-17-52.jpg
picks.what: View of the town, etching in Merian’s Topographia (Rijksmuseum)
picks.why: general view with St. Rumbold’s, the old St. Peter’s and a windmill, landmarks labeled; a thin sheet join runs just right of the cathedral; margins trimmed

picks.file: Thomas Shotter Boys (British - A View of the Church of Our Lady of Hanswijk, Mechelen (Malines), Belgium - Google Art Project.jpg
picks.what: The Church of Our Lady of Hanswijk on the Dyle, watercolor
picks.why: color view of the domed Hanswijk basilica over the river; signed and dated 1831

picks.file: Joseph Ignace van Hoey Malines Vue des canaux.jpg
picks.what: A canal lined with old houses, painting
picks.why: signed and dated town scene on one of the canals; no major landmark, but the only firmly dated later view

gaps: P0: nothing; P5: nothing usable; P6: no usable modern view
notes: The Braun and Hogenberg vol. 1 plate holds three panoramas (’s-Hertogenbosch, Leuven, Mechelen); #3 and #6 are bound spreads with the gutter through the views, #4 is a flat sheet. Vol. 3 (1581) plans (#1, #2, #5) are flat street plans. #10 (1682) is the same Braun and Hogenberg Mechelen strip reissued by Janssonius van Waesberge, so not a new view. #8 and #9 (van der Aa / ‘Les Forces de l’Europe’, about 1715–28) are a smaller, generic alternative for P2. #13 is dated only ‘early 19th century’; #14 (De Cauwer) only ‘before 1873’. #15 (Louis Titz, 1916) shows an unidentified church and is low-resolution. The 2021 photos (#16–#19) are a street, a car park meter and a snack bar.
